name: Castmagic
tagline: Turn a recording into a transcript, summary, clips, quotes, and reusable content assets

tiers.name: Hobby
tiers.limits: 30 transcribed library hours total; 3 spaces; 50 GB storage; 3 seats; 10 GB/file
tiers.notes: Billed $239/year; month-to-month price was not exposed on the current page. The supplied snapshot's $39/month headline no longer matches the live self-serve offer.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 100 transcribed library hours total; 10 spaces; 250 GB; 5 seats; API access
tiers.notes: Billed $579/year; month-to-month price was not exposed on the current page.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 400 transcribed library hours total; 25 spaces; 1 TB; 5 seats included; unlimited team size

tiers.name: Business & Scale
tiers.limits: Custom transcription volume, seats, storage, security and support
tiers.notes: Live promotional starting price is $699/month with $999 struck through.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no permanent free tier; a trial is offered, but its numeric allowance is not published on the live pricing page
pricing.billingTerms: annual self-serve plans (advertised as 30% lower) plus monthly/custom Business & Scale
pricing.hiddenCosts: Library-hour caps are cumulative rather than simple monthly allowances; more hours can be purchased, and Team seats beyond 5 cost $19/month or $159/year each.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Castmagic, turn a recording into a transcript, summary, clips, quotes, and reusable content assets. The hard boundary is large prompt library, integrations, team workflow, and hosted processing, plus audio infrastructure, distribution, and production polish.
coreLoopDIY: Import spoken-word audio, perform practical cleanup, generate a transcript, summary, clips, and quotes, and export production files plus show notes and reusable content assets.
whatYouLose: large prompt library, integrations, team workflow, and hosted processing
moatNotes: audio infrastructure, distribution, and production polish
ongoingBurden: codec support, loudness standards, transcription, storage, feeds, analytics, and deliverability to directories
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Castmagic because creators pay to remove fragile audio plumbing and publishing chores from a release schedule. The recurring cost buys codec support, loudness standards, transcription, storage, feeds, analytics, and deliverability to directories, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Audacity
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source multitrack audio editor and useful implementation prior art.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Speakr
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It handles transcripts and text assets, but not the audio or video clips in this job.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Hobby plan and a single-creator production tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Castmagic in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, ffmpeg, SQLite, and an HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import spoken-word audio, perform practical cleanup, generate a transcript, summary, clips, and quotes, and export production files plus show notes and reusable content assets.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create an upload queue and preserve originals in a read-only media folder.
Generate waveforms and non-destructive edit markers instead of rewriting source files.
Implement silence trimming, loudness normalization to -16 LUFS, fades, and noise-gate presets.
Add chapter markers, intro and outro slots, and a simple two-track timeline.
Produce a transcript and draft title, description, chapters, and social excerpts.
Export MP3, WAV, transcript, chapters JSON, and a complete project manifest.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out real-time remote recording.
Deliberately leave out podcast hosting and directory analytics.
Deliberately leave out licensed stock music and voice cloning.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
